title: Best of Bhutan FREE Visit to Taktsang Monastery
highlights: Experience the magic of Bhutan as you journey through Paro’s lush green valleys, Thimphu’s exquisite architecture & the breathtaking splendour of Punakha Dzong.
Hike to Tiger’s Nest (Taktsang) Monastery in Paro, perched 10,240 ft high on a cliff, where legend says Guru Rinpoche flew on a tigress’ back.
Stand before the majestic 177-ft Buddha Dordenma in Thimphu, enjoying stunning views of Thimphu Valley’s green hills and city skyline.
Feast your eyes on the unparalleled views from Dochula Pass, showcasing 108 chortens and Mt. Gangkhar Puensum, the world’s tallest unclimbed peak at 24,836 ft.
Explore Gangtey Monastery, renowned for its ancient architecture and stunning views of the Phobjikha Valley, home to the rare Black-Necked Cranes.

know_before_you_go: Images are for representation purpose only.

ID Proof is mandatory for each individual guest at the time of booking, and upon arrival. PAN Card will not be considered as a valid identity proof. All foreign nationals must carry their passport as a proof of identity.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.
To obtain entry in Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Plastic has been banned since 1999 in Bhutan, therefore, it is advised to carry plastic/plastic items.
Keep your arms and legs covered while visiting a Dzong (fortress-monastery).
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
In Bhutan, Tuesday is ‘Dry Day’. This means locals don’t drink alcohol on Tuesday. So it would be respectful to avoid alcohol on Tuesdays too.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Bhutan does not have a micro (or nano) SIM card. So check your mobile device for SIM compatibility before visiting Bhutan.
Ask your local guide to help you purchase a SIM on arrival, as Bhutan supports 2 networks: B-Mobile SIM and TashiCell.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.

meal_plans.name: Modified American Plan
meal_plans.description: Also known as Half Board or Half Pension meal plan. It is a modified version of the American Plan and includes a room stay with breakfast and a choice between lunch and dinner.

meal_plans.name: Continental Plan
meal_plans.description: It is where your room stay involves a daily breakfast at the hotel. The hotel can either affix its option of breakfast menu or provide in the dining area for a buffet breakfast. Also, whether the room service provides the breakfast or in a general dining area, depends from hotel to hotel.

meal_plans.name: European Plan
meal_plans.description: Only the stay is included in the rates and that you will have to pay extra for using the hotel’s dining facilities. This can be called the “Room Only” Plan.

days.desc: Upon arrival at Bagdogra International Airport/New Jalpaiguri Railway Station, you’ll be transferred to Phuntsholing, the border town of Bhutan. Later, get driven to the hotel and enjoy the rest of the day at leisure. You can visit Amo Chhu Crocodile Breeding Centre, home to various crocodile species or unwind at the Torsa Riverside. Return to the hotel on your own for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Thimphu | Leisure Day
days.desc: In the morning, check out and visit the immigration office to obtain the travel permit before being driven to Thimphu, Bhutan’s capital. Upon arrival, check in, relax, and then you can explore Thimphu’s attractions like the Royal Botanical Garden, known for its diverse flora, or stroll through the Ludrong Memorial Garden, which stands between Tashichho Dzong & Parliament House. The garden boasts various tree, shrub & flower species. Later, return to the hotel on your own for an overnight stay.

days.title: Thimphu Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Board your transfer & head to the Simtokha Dzong, one of Bhutan's oldest fortresses. Visit the Tashichho Dzong, a fortress-monastery that houses 30 temples, chapels and shrines and the Motithang Takin Preserve, home to Bhutan’s national animal, Takin. Explore the Handicraft Market & the National Memorial Chorten, a monument built in honour of the late King Jigme Dorji Wangchuck. Visit the 177-ft Buddha Dordenma Statue, overlooking the Thimphu Valley before getting driven back to the hotel.

days.title: Transfer to Punakha via Dochula Pass
days.desc: After checking out, get driven to Punakha, with a scenic stop at Dochula Pass to take in panoramic views of the snow-capped Himalayas. Next, visit Chimi Lhakhang, the "Temple of Fertility," built in 1499. Its most striking feature is the golden roof, gleaming in sunlight, with rows of prayer wheels. Continue to Punakha Dzong, a majestic fortress between Pho Chu and Mo Chu rivers, which once served as the seat of the government. Later, upon arrival at the hotel, check in for an overnight stay.

days.title: Day Trip to Gangtey
days.desc: Today, you will be driven to Gangtey on a day trip. Begin by visiting the Phobjikha Valley, a glacial valley renowned as the winter home to endangered black-necked cranes. Next, explore Gangtey Gompa, a 17th-century Nyingmapa monastery perched on a ridge, offering stunning valley views. Continue to Wangdue Phodrang Dzong, strategically located at the confluence of the Mo Chu and Tang Chu rivers. After your sightseeing tour, you'll be driven back to the hotel in Punakha for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Paro | Paro Sightseeing
days.desc: In the morning, check out of the hotel in Punakha and get driven to the beautiful town of Paro, passing through Bhutanese villages. Upon arrival, post check in, visit Kyichu Lhakhang, one of Bhutan’s oldest Buddhist temples, known for its vivid murals. Later, visit Drukgyel Dzong, a historic fortress that once protected Bhutan from Tibetan invasions. The dzong offers breathtaking views of Paro Valley & Mt. Jhomolhari, Bhutan’s 2nd highest peak. Get driven to the hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Hike to Tiger’s Nest Monastery
days.desc: In the morning, get driven to Ta Dzong, showcasing a rich collection of Bhutanese art, textiles, weapons & religious objects. Get ready for a trek to the Tiger’s Nest (Taktsang) Monastery & board the transfer to Satsam Chencho Tshongkhang. Pass by the pine forest & prayer flags to the monastery. Inside the monastery, explore prayer wheels, meditation caves & murals dedicated to Guru Rinpoche. After the descent, get transferred to the hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Phuntsholing | Stay & Sightseeing
days.desc: Today, check out and enjoy a scenic drive to Phuntsholing, on Bhutan’s southern border. Upon arrival, check in and begin your tour with a visit to the Bhutan Gate, a fine example of local craftsmanship. Explore Zangto Pelri Lhakhang, featuring intricate murals honouring Guru Rinpoche, then head to Karbandi Monastery for panoramic views of Phuntsholing & Bengal Plains. End the day at Phuntsholing Market, buzzing with local crafts and textiles, before returning to your hotel for an overnight stay.
